title: One rightward scan step
statement: Let $M$ be a Turing machine with no work tapes, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Suppose that for every work-tape reading, the transition from state $q$ on the $i$th bit of $x$ moves the input head right, leaves the work tapes unchanged, emits the optional bit $e$, and enters optional state $q'$. If $i<|x|$, then one step from the scan configuration at position $i$ in state $q$ with output $o$ gives the scan configuration at position $i+1$ in state $q'$ with output $o$ followed by $e$ when present.
hypotheses_covered: The transition condition holds for every work-tape reading
